briefs.research: Semrush India: 4,400 searches a month, KD 38, navigational intent. Zoho's own pricing page will hold position 1; aim for 2 to 5 with an angle Zoho will not publish.
briefs.audience: An Indian business owner or sales head comparing CRM costs before committing, usually with 5 to 25 people on the sales team.
briefs.angle: What Zoho CRM really costs in India over three years for a real team, priced from Zoho's own figures, and the honest point at which a custom CRM becomes the cheaper or better choice. Say plainly that for most small teams with a standard sales process, Zoho is the right answer.
briefs.title_hint: Zoho CRM Pricing in India: The 3-Year Cost for Your Team

facts.claim: Zoho CRM India prices, per user per month: Standard ₹800 billed yearly or ₹1,300 billed monthly; Professional ₹1,400 yearly or ₹2,100 monthly; Enterprise ₹2,400 yearly or ₹3,000 monthly; Ultimate ₹2,600 yearly or ₹3,200 monthly.
facts.source: https://www.zoho.com/crm/zohocrm-pricing.html (INR values read from Zoho's own pricing data file, crm-pricing-val.json)

facts.claim: Zoho CRM has a free edition. Third-party listings describe it as free for up to 3 users.
Zoho's pricing page offers a team-user add-on at ₹400 per user per month billed yearly, or ₹500 billed monthly.
Yaseen Khatib's published starting price for an AI-integrated CRM built around a team's own sales process is $2,000, one time, with the client owning the code. Smaller work is $15 to $30 an hour.

computed: Three years of Zoho CRM at yearly-billing prices (price x users x 36 months), before GST:
Paying monthly instead of yearly costs 62.5% more on Standard (₹1,300 vs ₹800) and 25% more on Enterprise (₹3,000 vs ₹2,400).
must_say: Prices change and are shown before GST; check Zoho's page and the final invoice before deciding.
For a small team with a standard sales process, Zoho (or its free edition) is usually the better choice. Say this clearly.
A custom CRM also has running costs (hosting, maintenance, someone to own it). Do not present the build price as the whole cost.
must_not: Do not invent implementation-partner fees, case studies, client names or results.
Do not quote any Zoho feature-by-edition detail that is not in the facts.
Do not compare with HubSpot, Salesforce or Freshsales prices; they are not in the facts.

briefs.research: DataForSEO US, 30 Oct 2026: 'lm studio vs ollama' 2,900 searches a month, KD 0; 'ollama vs lm studio' 1,600, KD 0; 'lmstudio vs ollama' 2,900, KD 0. A solo AI engineer's blog (zenvanriel.com) holds positions 7 to 9 with a plain comparison, so a first-hand, developer-angle comparison can reach the top 10.
briefs.audience: A developer or technical founder who wants to run an open model on their own machine and is choosing between the two most common tools.
briefs.angle: Which one a working developer should pick, decided by how you will talk to the model: a GUI for trying models versus a server other code calls. Draw on the author's own experience running Ollama on Windows for streamerOS (the linked streamerosai.com guide) and wiring local models into the local-first products on this site.
briefs.title_hint: Ollama vs LM Studio: Which One a Developer Should Run

facts.claim: Ollama is available for macOS, Windows and Linux, and as the official ollama/ollama Docker image.
Ollama runs a model with a single command, for example `ollama run gemma4`, and exposes a REST API on localhost port 11434 (for example http://localhost:11434/api/chat).
Ollama exposes an OpenAI-compatible API at http://localhost:11434/v1/ supporting a subset of the OpenAI API, including /v1/chat/completions, /v1/completions, /v1/embeddings and /v1/models.
LM Studio is available for macOS, Windows and Linux; it generally supports Apple Silicon Macs, x64/ARM64 Windows PCs and x64 Linux PCs.
LM Studio runs llama.cpp (GGUF) models on Mac, Windows and Linux, and MLX models on Apple Silicon Macs.
LM Studio can serve local models on OpenAI-like endpoints, locally and on the network, and ships a CLI named `lms` for chat, model downloads, daemon management, server control and publishing.

LM Studio has been free to use both at home and at work since 8 July 2025; company use previously required contacting LM Studio for a commercial licence, and that requirement was removed. Paid Teams and Enterprise plans exist for private sharing, SSO and gating.
The author has published a step-by-step guide to running Ollama on Windows on streamerosai.com.

must_say: Both are free for a developer; LM Studio's licence changed in July 2025, so older comparisons that call it non-commercial are out of date.
The practical difference is the entry point: LM Studio is a desktop app with a model browser and an optional server; Ollama is a server and CLI first, with no bundled chat window in the facts above.
Both expose OpenAI-compatible endpoints, so application code written against one can usually be pointed at the other.
must_not: Do not quote benchmark numbers, token speeds, memory usage or model sizes; none are in the facts.
Do not state LM Studio's server port or Ollama's licence; neither is in the facts.
Do not invent feature lists beyond the sourced ones.
